newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.

text.p: For the week of June 9, here are some of the top stories reported in major U.S. technology trade publications.

PC WEEK - Microsoft Corp's plan to activate the Internet and turn ActiveX into a standard isn't nearly as active as supporters had hoped, and slow progress by the Active Group standards body, combined with security concerns, has kept ActiveX from making significant inroads, PC Week reported June 9.
Apache, a new free Web server software program developed by a small group of dispersed UNIX developers, has become the most popular Web server software on the Internet, PC Week reported June 9.

COMPUTERWORLD - Amdahl Corp hopes to steal some thunder from IBM's long-expected mainframe processor upgrade announcement this week as it tries to one-up IBM by outlining its own upgrade plans for the next three years, Computerworld reported June 9.

When Netscape Communications Corp introduces the commercial version of its Communicator client software at a developers conference this week, the one-time Internet wunderkind will face a far more skeptical user audience than ever before, Computerworld reported June 9.

COMPUTER RESELLER NEWS - The NEC Computer Systems Division of Packard Bell NEC Inc is considering a plan to pull its desktop and notebook PCs from distributors and begin selling direct to end users in August - a move that resellers said could threaten NEC Technologies Inc's monitor and peripherals business, Computer Reseller News reported June 9.

Microsoft this month will release the first beta version of Memphis, its next upgrade of its Windows 95, which the company says will incorporate Internet Explorer 4.0, Computer Reseller News reported June 9. But few of the recent daily builds, which Microsoft delivered to testers in the past few months, have included an integrated browser, CRN reported.

INFOWORLD - Intel Corp is considering a new reference platform for a $1,000 personal computer separate from the network computer and its NetPC initiative with partner Microsoft, InfoWorld reported June 9.

Microsoft's answer to network computers, a software project code-named Hydra, will enter beta testing by year-end and will include a server, a thin client and a protocol to operate remote machines, InfoWorld reported.

INFORMATION WEEK - The battle between Java and ActiveX is shaping up into a nasty war as Microsoft refuses to back Sun Microsystems Inc's "100 percent Pure Java" initiative, Information Week reported June 9.

Separately, Sun will unveil plans next week to provide different version of its Solaris operating system for enterprises, intranets and the Internet, Information Week said in a report attributed to unidentified sources.

EE TIMES - Despite recent talk of a delayed takeoff for PCs equipped with DVD (digital video disk), both computer and higher-priced standalone consumer DVD drives were the main buzz at an otherwise lackluster Spring Comdex show last week, EE Times reported June 9.

Two new embedded DRAM camps were formed last week when LSI Logic and Micron Technology Inc agreed to develop a stacked cell embedded DRAM process, while Toshiba Corp licensed its trench-cell process to Singapore's Chartered Semiconductor Manufacturing Ltd, for the development of new memory chips, EE Times reported June 9.

ELECTRONIC BUYERS' NEWS - PC Makers and board vendors can begin developing DVD-equipped PCs for the Christmas selling season, now that a key decoding license has been granted by Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd which controls the technology behind DVD's Content Scrambling System, Electronic Buyers' News reported on June 9.

MACWEEK - As Apple Computer Inc's latest entry in the subnotebook class waits at the starting line, sources said that the company is on track with two new PowerBooks, code named Kanga and Wall Street, to be based on the PowerPC G3 processor, MacWeek reported June 9. Kanga is expected in October and Wall Street will appear in the first half of 1998, MacWeek reported.
